tl;dr: how do I make docs#WithVal.instRing un-unfoldable (other than perhaps in the file it's defined in), and WithVal.instCommRing and WithVal.instField only unfoldable as far as WithVal.instRing?

Here's a funny thing (it is the root cause of something which is making FLT slow).

import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Valued.WithVal

variable (K Γ₀ : Type*) [LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero Γ₀] [Field K] (v : Valuation K Γ₀)

#synth Field (WithVal v) -- WithVal.instField v
#synth CommRing (WithVal v) -- WithVal.instCommRing v

-- to see the results below, uncomment these
-- set_option trace.profiler.useHeartbeats true
-- set_option trace.profiler true

example :  (WithVal.instField v).toCommRing = WithVal.instCommRing v := rfl
-- [definition.value] [3792.000000] ✅️ _example ▼

example :  (WithVal.instField v).toCommRing.toRing = (WithVal.instCommRing v).toRing := rfl
-- [definition.value] [5369.000000] ✅️ _example ▶

example :  (WithVal.instField v).toCommRing.toRing.toAddGroupWithOne =
    (WithVal.instCommRing v).toRing.toAddGroupWithOne := rfl
-- [definition.value] [57012.000000] ✅️ _example ▶

In the above file I create two instances i1 and i2 (namely (WithVal.instField v).toCommRing.toRing and (WithVal.instCommRing v).toRing) and I observe that typeclass inference takes 10 times longer to check i1.toAddGroupWithOne = i2.toAddGroupWithOne than it does to check i1 = i2. The reason for this is that AddGroupWithOne is not a "preferred parent" of Ring and the typeclass inference algorithm decides to check i1.toAddGroupWithOne = i2.toAddGroupWithOne by unfolding both i1 and i2, which in this situation is expensive.

trace of the disaster

[] [25681.000000] ✅️ (WithVal.instField v).toAddGroupWithOne =?= (WithVal.instCommRing v).toAddGroupWithOne ▼
        [] [25392.000000] ✅️ { toIntCast := (WithVal.instField v).toIntCast, toNatCast := (WithVal.instField v).toNatCast,
              toAddMonoid := (WithVal.instField v).toAddMonoid, toOne := (WithVal.instField v).toOne, natCast_zero := ⋯,
              natCast_succ := ⋯, toNeg := (WithVal.instField v).toNeg, toSub := (WithVal.instField v).toSub,
              sub_eq_add_neg := ⋯, zsmul := Ring.zsmul, zsmul_zero' := ⋯, zsmul_succ' := ⋯, zsmul_neg' := ⋯,
              neg_add_cancel := ⋯, intCast_ofNat := ⋯,
              intCast_negSucc :=
                ⋯ } =?= { toIntCast := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toIntCast,
              toNatCast := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toNatCast, toAddMonoid := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toAddMonoid,
              toOne := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toOne, natCast_zero := ⋯, natCast_succ := ⋯,
              toNeg := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toNeg, toSub := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toSub, sub_eq_add_neg := ⋯,
              zsmul := Ring.zsmul, zsmul_zero' := ⋯, zsmul_succ' := ⋯, zsmul_neg' := ⋯, neg_add_cancel := ⋯,
              intCast_ofNat := ⋯, intCast_negSucc := ⋯ } ▼
          [] [3457.000000] ✅️ Ring.zsmul =?= Ring.zsmul ▶
          [] [639.000000] ✅️ WithVal v =?= WithVal v ▶
          [] [3448.000000] ✅️ (WithVal.instField v).toIntCast =?= (WithVal.instCommRing v).toIntCast ▶
          [] [10682.000000] ✅️ { toNatCast := (WithVal.instField v).toNatCast, toAddMonoid := (WithVal.instField v).toAddMonoid,
                toOne := (WithVal.instField v).toOne, natCast_zero := ⋯,
                natCast_succ :=
                  ⋯ } =?= { toNatCast := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toNatCast,
                toAddMonoid := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toAddMonoid, toOne := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toOne,
                natCast_zero := ⋯, natCast_succ := ⋯ } ▶
          [] [3355.000000] ✅️ (WithVal.instField v).toNeg =?= (WithVal.instCommRing v).toNeg ▶
          [] [3401.000000] ✅️ (WithVal.instField v).toSub =?= (WithVal.instCommRing v).toSub ▶

I complained about this here #lean4 > instance explosion @ 💬 and nobody reacted, so I experimented with changing Lean's typeclass inference system so that it would no longer do this, and it turned out that all the patches I made to core Lean made my issue above quicker but made other typeclass searches (especially failing ones) slower (and ultimately made mathlib slower), so I gave up on that approach.

I would like to propose another approach here, but my understanding of private/expose and the module system is not good enough for me to be anything but vague.

What is happening here is that WithVal (v : Valuation K Γ₀) is a one-field structure and a moral type synonym for K. Note also that Valuation K Γ₀ demands Ring K, and these instances like WithVal.instCommRing etc just pull back a CommRing K to CommRing (WithVal v) (or Ring or Field) via WithVal.equiv v : WithVal v ≃+* K.

Nowadays defeq abuse is strongly not allowed, and the reason WithVal v is a one-field structure is to encourage this. My instinct is that it is thus never correct to unfold WithVal.instRing in a file downstream from its definition, because the only possible answer is "it's come from the ring structure on K and you are not really supposed to be using this fact". And yet this is exactly what rfl is doing in the above example (and exactly what typeclass inference is doing both in mathlib already and also all over a corner of FLT in files which will one day be PRed to mathlib but which I'm too embarrassed to PR right now because they are so slow).

Can I somehow use a combination of seal/unseal/module/no_expose (I only have the vaguest understanding of what these thing do currently, but am eager to learn) to stop the explosion from happening?
What happens if you attribute [irreducible] WithVal.instRing and then accept the set_option you need do make it work in the current file?
you actually do want to unfold WithVal.instRing sometimes, to check for defeq with docs#WithVal.instSMul_1

To my surprise, making it irreducible makes things worse. On today's mathlib I'm seeing

[definition.value] [64208.000000] ✅️ _example ▶

for the slow (third) example above on master, and if I write attribute [irreducible] WithVal.instRing at the bottom of Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Valued.WithVal and recompile the test file above it goes up to [definition.value] [85495.000000] ✅️ _example ▶. Comparing the traces, the explosion is still occurring and this check

          [] [12772.000000] ✅️ { toNatCast := (WithVal.instField v).toNatCast, toAddMonoid := (WithVal.instField v).toAddMonoid,
                toOne := (WithVal.instField v).toOne, natCast_zero := ⋯,
                natCast_succ :=
                  ⋯ } =?= { toNatCast := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toNatCast,
                toAddMonoid := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toAddMonoid, toOne := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toOne,
                natCast_zero := ⋯, natCast_succ := ⋯ } ▶

on master now goes up to 26271. Everything is still being unfolded though.

Kevin Buzzard said:

Nowadays defeq abuse is strongly not allowed, and the reason WithVal v is a one-field structure is to encourage this

Making things a one-field structure doesn't just discourage it; I'd argue it already makes it completely impossible.

By additionally making the ring instance irreducible, you're saying that using the defeq WithVal.ofVal (x + y) = WithVal.ofVal x + WithVal.ofVal y is also not allowed; but to me this is quite clearly defeq use not defeq abuse
(having lemmas like these be defeq is one of the things that makes dsimp be useful)

I still don't know the answer to the question "how do I stop typeclass inference from exploding the instance", I'm just hearing various conjectures from people about why it might be a bad idea to do so, and one failed suggestion. I would like to try nonetheless! I would be tempted to suggest that WithVal.ofVal (x + y) never occurs in mathlib (other than perhaps in an unused API lemma) but I might be completely wrong.

Experimenting with Claude and it's now telling me that all of the tools we have are not capable of doing this; if typeclass inference wants to unfold WithVal.instRing then it will, and in particular if typeclass inference is faced with i1.toAddGroupWithOne = i2.toAddGroupWithOne with i1 and i2 not syntactically identical then there is literally nothing available to me to stop typeclass infererence from unfolding i1 and i2. I am not sure I believe this. Is this the situation we are currently in?
Unification hint? Hmm, too generic I think here

Oh I am so confused. attribute [local irreducible] WithVal.instRing does have a positive effect in FLT. It just has a negative effect in the MWE above.

import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Valued.WithVal

variable (K Γ₀ : Type*) [LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero Γ₀] [Field K] (v : Valuation K Γ₀)

set_option trace.profiler.useHeartbeats true
set_option trace.profiler true

example :  (WithVal.instField v).toCommRing.toRing.toAddGroupWithOne =
    (WithVal.instCommRing v).toRing.toAddGroupWithOne := rfl
-- [definition.value] [57007.000000] ✅️ _example ▶

attribute [local irreducible] WithVal.instRing in
example :  (WithVal.instField v).toCommRing.toRing.toAddGroupWithOne =
    (WithVal.instCommRing v).toRing.toAddGroupWithOne := rfl
-- [definition.value] [85279.000000] ✅️ _example ▶

Oh I do see now. The explosion is still taking place, it's just a different kind of explosion :-/

[] [43274.000000] ✅️ (WithVal.instCommRing v).toAddGroupWithOne =?= (WithVal.instField v).toAddGroupWithOne ▼

[] [42821.000000] ✅️ { toIntCast := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toIntCast, toNatCast := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toNatCast, toAddMonoid := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toAddMonoid, toOne := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toOne, natCast_zero := ⋯, natCast_succ := ⋯, toNeg := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toNeg, toSub := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toSub, sub_eq_add_neg := ⋯, zsmul := Ring.zsmul, zsmul_zero' := ⋯, zsmul_succ' := ⋯, zsmul_neg' := ⋯, neg_add_cancel := ⋯, intCast_ofNat := ⋯, intCast_negSucc := ⋯ } =?= { toIntCast := (WithVal.instField v).toIntCast, toNatCast := (WithVal.instField v).toNatCast, toAddMonoid := (WithVal.instField v).toAddMonoid, toOne := (WithVal.instField v).toOne, natCast_zero := ⋯, natCast_succ := ⋯, toNeg := (WithVal.instField v).toNeg, toSub := (WithVal.instField v).toSub, sub_eq_add_neg := ⋯, zsmul := Ring.zsmul, zsmul_zero' := ⋯, zsmul_succ' := ⋯, zsmul_neg' := ⋯, neg_add_cancel := ⋯, intCast_ofNat := ⋯, intCast_negSucc := ⋯ } ▼

The instance never gets unfolded, but the explosion occurs anyway.
Does dropping the use of Equiv.ring and building things manually with Function.Injective.ring help at all?

It is definitely possible to achieve what you want with the visibility system. Anything you don't want to unfold should be hidden behind a public non-exposed def. Anything you might want to unfold can be given as a field the usual way

Unfortunately Matt's answer (now that I finally understand it) has shown me that this doesn't solve the problem. The actual problem is that (a) Ring.toAddGroupWithOne is a mess (it extracts and recreates 7 new data fields) (b) Lean insists on proving i1.toAddGroupWithOne =?= i2.toAddGroupWithOne by unfolding Ring.toAddGroupWithOne even if proving i1 = i2 is trivial.

Making WithVal.instRing irreducible still means that faced with the goal i1.toAddGroupWithOne = i2.toAddGroupWithOne we are doomed to have to prove i1.toIntCast = i2.toIntCast, i1.toNatCast = i2.toNatCast, i1.toAddMonoid = i2.toAddMonoid, i1.toOne = i2.toOne, i1.toNeg = i2.toNeg, i1.toSub = i2.toSub and i1.zsmul = i2.zsmul.

import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Valued.WithVal

variable {K Γ₀ : Type*} [LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero Γ₀] [Field K] (v : Valuation K Γ₀)

-- set_option trace.profiler.useHeartbeats true
-- set_option trace.profiler true

abbrev i1 : Ring (WithVal v) := (WithVal.instField v).toCommRing.toRing
abbrev i2 : Ring (WithVal v) := (WithVal.instCommRing v).toRing

/-
  [definition.value] [6234.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
-/
example : i1 v = i2 v := rfl

/-
  [definition.value] [6260.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
-/
attribute [local irreducible] WithVal.instRing in
example : i1 v = i2 v := rfl

-- you're damned if you do
attribute [local irreducible] WithVal.instRing in
/-
  [definition.value] [85263.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
-/
example : (WithVal.instField v).toCommRing.toRing.toAddGroupWithOne =
    (WithVal.instCommRing v).toRing.toAddGroupWithOne := rfl

-- and you're damned if you don't
/-
  [definition.value] [65486.000000] ✅️ _example ▶
-/
example : (i1 v).toAddGroupWithOne = (i2 v).toAddGroupWithOne := rfl

Kevin Buzzard said:

The actual problem is that (a) Ring.toAddGroupWithOne is a mess (it extracts and recreates 7 new data fields) (b) Lean insists on proving i1.toAddGroupWithOne =?= i2.toAddGroupWithOne by unfolding Ring.toAddGroupWithOne even if proving i1 = i2 is trivial.

Making WithVal.instRing irreducible still means that faced with the goal i1.toAddGroupWithOne = i2.toAddGroupWithOne we are doomed to have to prove i1.toIntCast = i2.toIntCast, i1.toNatCast = i2.toNatCast, i1.toAddMonoid = i2.toAddMonoid, i1.toOne = i2.toOne, i1.toNeg = i2.toNeg, i1.toSub = i2.toSub and i1.zsmul = i2.zsmul.

But surely doing something trivial 7 times can't take much longer than doing it once?

Doing something trivial 7000 times takes longer than doing it 1000 times but doing something slightly less trivial 7000 times takes even longer, which is why making it irreducible in FLT does help. The issue is that if you're developing the theory of valuations of fields then you're doing this all the time.

OK I have made a PR #39519 which I think both good and bad. Right now it's a draft: it makes WithVal.instRing irreducible and then uses set_option allowUnsafeReducibility to fix the three proofs which broke. The good thing is that it is a 117G speed-up (including 20% speedup in two files for which we have a lot of potential extra material in FLT/Mathlib but which I am hesitating to PR because I am not happy with how long typeclass inference is taking). The allowUnsafeReducibility hacks I can fix by rewriting proofs. What I am worried about is the comments about dsimp etc above. I remember Mario telling me back in the Lean 3 days that the following is bad: (1) make a thing (2) prove API about it using rfl (3) make it irreducible. Because then rfl no longer works, and somehow that is bad. Is that still the case in Lean 4? Is #39519 the correct thing to do? Because I absolutely want to do it downstream in FLT but I don't want to do it if it's somehow illegal/unwise.
If the proof is by rfl instead of rfl then all is good again and you can ignore Mario's complaint
Right, which is the same as declaring that dsimp is not allowed to do anything useful to WithVal

And is that ok or not?

I guess the places where mathlib broke after I made it irreducible are the places where this defeq is being used. In FLT nothing breaks if I make it irreducible.

I think it's a slippery slope which leads to the death of the dsimp tactic. The defeq you're banning here is pretty much the most harmless defeq possible, and so this stance only seems justifiable to me if the goal is to ban _all_ defeqs.
In this particular instance it's saying "it is more costly to unfold to check for defeq than it is to force lean not to unfold, because inside there is a big term and it's always the same big term"
